info.name: TicTac — licences, billing and onboarding
info.description:
Manual test collection for the TicTac backend.

## Run order

Folders are numbered. Run them top to bottom the first time — later requests depend on variables captured by earlier ones (`ownerAccessToken`, `organizationId`, `invitationToken`, …).

## Emails are generated per run

A collection pre-request script sets `runId` once and derives `ownerEmail` / `inviteeEmail` from it, so registering twice does not collide. **To start a completely fresh run, delete the `runId` collection variable.** To use your own addresses, set `ownerEmail` / `inviteeEmail` in the ENVIRONMENT — environment values win over collection ones.

## What needs Stripe

Folders 01–03 work against a bare local server. Folders 04–06 need billing configured and a live subscription. See `postman/README.md` in the repo for both the Stripe CLI route and a SQL shortcut that skips Stripe entirely.

## Requests that are SUPPOSED to fail

Anything named `(negative)` asserts a 4xx. They are the interesting ones: they prove a non-member gets 404 rather than 403, that an invitation cannot be replayed, and that money cannot be spent by the wrong person.

Emails are generated per run (see the collection pre-request script), so this can be re-run without hitting `409 Email already registered`. To start a completely fresh run, clear the `runId` collection variable.

request.description: Resolves the token's `sub` to a live account. The user id is never taken from the request.
Rotates BOTH tokens. The old refresh token is now spent — replaying it is treated as theft and revokes every session for that user, so do not run this twice in a row with a stale value.

item.name: 02 · Organization

request.description:
The caller becomes OWNER in the same transaction. An organization with no owner is unfixable through the API, so the two are never separate.

It starts holding **one licence** — the free included one — and has no Stripe customer or subscription at all.
One member for now: the owner, occupying the free included licence.

item.name: Another tenant is a 404, not a 403 (negative)

request.description: A non-member gets 404. A 403 here would turn a leaked organization id into an existence oracle for that tenant.

item.description: Creating the tenant everything else hangs off.

item.name: 03 · Licences — the free organization

request.description: A brand-new organization: 1 licence held, 1 member occupying it, 0 vacant, 0 billed.
'Never subscribed' is a state, not a 404. `status` is absent and `billing` is false, but the organization still holds its included licence.

**Expected to fail.** The one included licence is occupied by the owner, and there is no card on file to buy another — so the licence cannot be acquired.

Note the refusal happens at INVITE time, not acceptance: the administrator finds out at the moment they decide, and no dead link goes out.

exec: pm.expect(b.title).to.eql('No subscription to add a licence to');

request.description: **Expected to fail.** Licences are added to an existing subscription; the first purchase must go through checkout, because there is no card yet.

item.description:
What a brand-new organization looks like, and the two things it cannot do yet.

Both negatives here are the point of the model: nothing is gated except headcount, and headcount needs a card.

item.name: 04 · Stripe — checkout and portal

request.description:
Buys the organization's FIRST licences. `licenses` is the total it will hold, so Stripe's quantity is 4 — the first licence is included free.

**This activates nothing.** It returns a URL to send a browser to. The subscription becomes real only when Stripe confirms over a signed webhook.

Open `checkoutUrl` from the collection variables in a browser and pay with the test card `4242 4242 4242 4242`, any future expiry, any CVC.

exec: pm.test('quantity excludes the free licence', function () {

request.description: Same thing on the annual price. The interval is chosen once, here, and every later licence change leaves it alone.

**OWNER only** — narrower than licence management, because this is cards, invoices and cancellation rather than headcount.

No request body. Creates the Stripe customer if the organization does not have one yet, so this works even before any purchase.

⚠️ Stripe returns an error until you have SAVED the portal configuration once, in Dashboard → Settings → Billing → Customer portal. See the collection README; a `502 Billing provider error` here almost always means that.

item.name: An admin cannot open the portal (negative)

request.description: Run this after the invitee has joined and been promoted to ADMIN. An ADMIN may buy and change licences but not touch the payment instrument.

item.name: Stripe webhook (reference only — do not send by hand)

request.description:
**Do not fire this from Postman.** The endpoint's entire authentication is an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body, so an unsigned request is correctly rejected with 400.

To receive real events locally:

```
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8080/api/webhooks/stripe
```

Copy the `whsec_...` it prints into `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and restart the app. Completing a checkout then writes the subscription and raises `license_count`.

item.description:
Checkout captures a card ONCE. Everything after it — more licences, fewer licences — is `PUT /licenses`, which charges the saved card with no redirect.

**Nothing in folders 05–07 will work until a subscription actually exists.** Either complete a checkout with the Stripe CLI listening, or use the SQL shortcut in the README.

item.name: 05 · Licences — with a subscription

request.description: After a completed checkout for 5: 5 held, 1 occupied, 4 vacant, 4 billed.

**No checkout, no redirect, no card re-entry.** Stripe charges the card on file and prorates for the rest of the period — monthly or annual alike.

The body is the whole count, not a delta, so sending it twice does nothing the second time.
Idempotent: the count is set, never incremented, so Stripe is not called at all.

**Expected to fail** — with 400, because 0 licences is not a thing: the free included licence always exists. To stop paying entirely, ask for `1`, which cancels.

For the 409 version, get two members into the organization first (folder 06) and then try to reduce to 1.

Giving up the last paid licence CANCELS the subscription rather than leaving it at quantity zero — Stripe does not treat zero as reliably free, and it still reads as paid in the dashboard.

⚠️ Run this last. Coming back means checking out again.

item.description:
These need a live subscription — see folder 04.

The rule being demonstrated: **the licence count only ever moves because somebody asked it to.** Members joining and leaving never touch it.

item.name: 06 · Invitations — adding a user

request.description:
OWNER or ADMIN. **This is where money moves**: if a licence is vacant the invitee will reuse it for free; if none is, one is acquired now and Stripe's quantity goes up by one.

The raw token is returned in the response only because email delivery does not exist yet — it is never stored and never logged. It is captured into `invitationToken`.

An invitation always grants MEMBER. There is no role field, deliberately: letting an inviter choose would let an ADMIN mint an ADMIN through a side door.

request.description: `pendingInvitations` is 1, and `licensesAvailable` has dropped even though nobody has joined yet: **an outstanding invitation holds a licence**. Without that, two invitations issued back to back would both be promised the same vacant licence.

exec: pm.test('the invitation is holding a licence', function () {

request.description:
**Expected to fail.** The invitation was issued to `{{inviteeEmail}}`; an account cannot be created at a different address on the back of it.

Run this BEFORE the accept above, while the invitation is still unconsumed.

**Public** — no Authorization header. Creates the account and consumes the invitation in one transaction.

`email` is required and must match the address the invitation was issued to — a mismatch is 422. It is not proof of identity (possession of the token is what proves you have the link); it is asked for because creating an account needs every field registration needs, and it is checked so an account cannot be created at a different address than the one invited.

There is deliberately **no `organizationId`** — that comes off the invitation row, so there is no parameter to steer an acceptance into another tenant.

Use this OR the next request, not both — an invitation is single-use.

**Authenticated** — the caller's own email must be the invited one, compared against the account behind a verified token and never against anything in the body.

This lives on the authenticated chain on purpose: the public POST chain ignores the Authorization header entirely, so acceptance-as-an-existing-user cannot live there.

Use this only if the invitee already had an account — otherwise use the request above.
Captures `inviteeAccessToken` so the negative authorization checks elsewhere can run.
**Expected to fail.** Acceptance is single-use, serialised by a row lock on the invitation.
Two members occupying, one fewer vacant, and **`billedLicenses` is unchanged** — the licence was paid for when the invitation went out, not when it was accepted.
An invitation only ever grants MEMBER, so a new administrator is invited and then promoted. OWNER is never assignable this way — moving ownership is its own operation.

item.name: Remove the member — vacates, does not un-buy

request.description:
**The rule that matters most.** The licence becomes vacant and the organization keeps paying for it, so the next person moves straight into it with nothing to buy.

Check `GET /licenses` afterwards: `membersOccupying` drops, `licenseCount` and `billedLicenses` do not.
One vacant licence, still billed. Re-run 'Invite a user' with a different address and watch it be reused for free — no Stripe call at all.

exec: pm.test('a licence is now vacant', function () {

item.description:
The full onboarding round trip: invite → accept → promote → remove.

Needs a live subscription with a spare licence (folder 04). Use EITHER 'registers AND accepts' OR '…existing user accepts' — an invitation is single-use.

item.name: 07 · Projects and time tracking

request.description: Organization membership grants nothing at project level. Administrators can reach every project without being assigned, but tracking time is a separate question.
A category is a KIND of work, not a unit of work — this is a time tracker, not a task manager.
`startedAt` is server time — no request DTO anywhere accepts a timestamp or a duration, so a client-supplied value has nowhere to land.
A running timer is just a row with `ended_at IS NULL`. Elapsed time is computed on read; the browser is never the source of truth.

item.name: Everything still works with no subscription

request.description: Worth running after cancelling in folder 05. **There are no paid features** — a cancelled organization has exactly the same functionality as a paying one. The only thing money buys is licences.

item.description: Not billing, but useful for proving the point that nothing here is gated by the subscription.

item.name: 08 · Teardown

request.description: Public POST, and the chain deliberately ignores any Authorization header: clients attach their access token to everything, and a STALE one must not fail authentication before logout can run — which is exactly when logout matters.

OWNER only. Soft delete — the row is tombstoned and nothing is destroyed: memberships, projects, time entries and the licence count all survive. There is no restore and no purge.

**Any active subscription stops renewing**, in the same transaction. At period end by default — the customer has already paid for it — so `cancelAtPeriodEnd` becomes true while the status stays ACTIVE until Stripe actually ends it.

It has to happen here: afterwards every billing endpoint 404s, because the tenant is gone. Check with the next request.

Run 'Login owner' again first if the logout above already spent the session.

The opt-in alternative: ends the subscription on the spot and Stripe credits the unused remainder, rather than letting the paid period run out.

Use this OR the request above, not both — the second one 404s, because the organization is already gone.
**Expected to fail.** A deleted tenant is a 404 to everyone, including its owner — which is exactly why cancellation happens during the delete rather than being left for later.

item.description:
Deleting an organization also stops its subscription renewing — at period end by default, immediately with `?cancelImmediately=true`.

Clearing the `runId` collection variable is usually enough to start clean without deleting anything.
